title: Increasing energy efficiency in industrial plants: Optimising heat exchanger networks
contribution: MEng report (Miten Mistry, supervised by Ruth Misener) proving that the reciprocal of the log mean temperature difference has a C2 extension and is strictly convex, and using this to build a binary-free tangent outer approximation inside an iteratively refined MILP relaxation of the Yee-Grossmann heat exchanger network MINLP, evaluated on three MINLPLib2 instances.
problem_entry: LMTD in heat exchanger network synthesis is indeterminate at equal approach temperatures and is routinely replaced by the Chen approximation or an epsilon-shift that introduce error; the project removes that approximation and aims at a globally convergent MILP-based scheme (pp. 3, 12, 37-39).
key_idea: Approximate the reciprocal m = ln(x/y)/(x-y) instead of LMTD (errors otherwise cascade through a denominator), prove m strictly convex, and refine a MILP (nf4r McCormick, PLF for A^beta, tangent OA for m) by adding mirrored tangents at the active exchangers' solution points (pp. 42, 61-62, 71-80).
assumptions: x, y > 0 in per-exchanger boxes [dTmin, T_i^in - T_j^in]; the model pushes area and hence m downward so >= tangents are tight; exact global MILP solver and a priori partition counts fixed from an objective tolerance (pp. 42, 76-77, 79, 89).
proof_devices: polar coordinates collapse the indeterminate line x = y to theta = pi/4; separable p(r)q1(theta)/q2(theta) plus L'Hopital gives lim m = 1/c (pp. 44-48)
C2 extension of m, grad m, Hessian m defined from the limits (Def. 3.1, pp. 48-49)
symmetry lemma m(x,y) = m(y,x) halves the domain (Lemma 3.1, p. 50)
directional derivative along (-1,1) and monotonicity give box bounds 1/u and 1/l on the diagonal (Prop. 3.1-3.3, pp. 51-56)
Hessian definiteness via leading principal minors in w = x/y with substitution w = e^n and sign arguments from derivatives at n = 0 (Prop. 3.4-3.5, pp. 56-62)
nf4r partitioned McCormick shown equivalent to McCormick on the active subinterval by substitution (p. 75)
non-termination counterexample sequence c + 1/i motivating epsilon-termination (p. 80)
error-cascade graph and convex-combination split of the objective tolerance to derive partition counts N*_beta, N*_A, N*_q (pp. 82, 89-93)
experiments: Gurobi 6.0.3 on one desktop; MINLPLib2 heatexch_gen1-3 with best-known solutions and LINDO/BARON/SCIP lower bounds; N in {1,10,...,50}; at most 10 iterations, Model 3 up to 32224 s; N=1 bounds beat solver lower bounds on Models 1-2; Model 2 bound exceeds the best-known solution (attributed to numerical error); heuristic sum_k z_ijk <= 1 cuts time 71%/82% on Models 1-2 only (pp. 66, 97-105).
positioning: Builds on the Yee-Grossmann/Escobar-Grossmann stage-wise model (corrected against GAMS), criticises Chen and epsilon approaches, credits Zavala-Rio et al. for prior LMTD proofs, reuses Gounaris-Misener-Floudas nf4r and the APOGEE presentation (pp. 37-41, 73, 111, 116-118).
writing: Student report: long textbook background, full algebraic proofs with plots before each property, bulleted contributions; abstract overclaims ('The first of its kind') while the evaluation states plainly that the algorithm fails to scale (pp. 3, 12-13, 15-31, 99).
limits_future: A priori partitioning creates binaries that block scaling and equal-width partitions miss the global optimum; future work: adaptive refinement, spatial branch and bound, a convex formulation for MINLP solvers (pp. 99, 104, 107-108); unstated: convergence relies on exact MILP solves and an informal tangent step (pp. 89, 94).

method_links.note: Student voice: plot LMTD's reciprocal, see it looks convex, prove it, exploit it with tangent cuts; talk title 'Special Structure Detection'; concrete case behind Method 1 step 2.

PLF vs OA chosen by fit with the other relaxations in the full model (all under-estimators, no extra binaries, no reformulation per iteration), not by isolated quality; thin evidence (three instances, simplified model).

Partition count N interpolates from plain McCormick (N=1) to tighter relaxations and is swept with time cost reported, but one N for all relaxations, no selection rule beyond the a priori error budget, parameter not removed.

Student voice: an invalid bound above the best-known solution on Model 2 is put down to numerical error without re-runs; no competitors run on the same hardware. In its favour: published model audited against GAMS and corrected; losses written in.

new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Approximate 1/LMTD, which multiplies q, rather than LMTD, which divides it, so approximation error does not cascade through a denominator; the reciprocal turns out convex.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: proved continuous extension instead of epsilon-shift
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Indeterminacy at x = y removed by proving limits of m and its derivatives and defining a C2 extension, replacing Chen/epsilon approaches that add error.
Escobar-Grossmann model compared with its GAMS specification; sign, quantifier, inequality-direction and naming errors corrected with an equation-by-equation change log.

transferable: Approximate the function whose error enters the model linearly and that the model pushes toward the side where tangent cuts are tight (p. 42).
Remove a removable singularity with polar coordinates and L'Hopital and ship the C2 extension instead of an epsilon-shift (pp. 44-49).
Prove 2x2 Hessian definiteness for a function of a ratio by reducing minors to functions of w = x/y and substituting w = e^n (pp. 56-61).
Seed an outer approximation with tangents at the diagonal box corners so cut bounds equal the function's exact bounds, and mirror tangent points to keep symmetry (pp. 76-78).
Keep all relaxations pointing the same way (all under-estimators) so every refinement raises the bound monotonically (p. 69).
Split an objective tolerance across term groups along an error-cascade graph to derive partition counts for a fixed-precision MILP relaxation (pp. 82, 89-93).
Evaluate a bounding algorithm on instances with both best-known solutions and published solver lower bounds, plotting objective by iteration against the best-known value (pp. 97, 102-103).
Keep an equation-by-equation change log when correcting a published model against its GAMS file (pp. 116-118).
coauthors: Miten Mistry (author, MEng student); Ruth Misener (supervisor); Panos Parpas (second marker)

quotes.text: We see from Figure 3.1 that the reciprocal of LMTD has a shape that looks convex (where defined, the epigraph looks convex), we will not only prove that this is true but we will use this to form a suitable approximation.
We find that, as it stands, the algorithm fails to scale in the directions that we want it to scale.
